reconciled_candidates.label: Monte Carlo Simulation for Risk Assessment
reconciled_candidates.description: Stochastic modeling uses probability distributions to simulate risk factors, generating a full distribution of outcomes rather than a single point estimate, enabling more informed decision-making.
coverage_criteria: Explain how Monte Carlo simulation differs from deterministic modeling, and describe the steps: defining distributions, running iterations, and interpreting a frequency histogram of outcomes.
reconciled_candidates.merge_rationale: Both candidates describe the fundamental difference between deterministic and stochastic approaches and the core Monte Carlo method; they together form one teachable concept.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The article explicitly presents Monte Carlo simulation as the core of its methodology (Sections 3.3 and 4) and demonstrates its application with Crystal Ball on two projects, generating profit distributions.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: This concept is a single, well-defined method that can be taught as a standalone risk assessment technique.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The introduction (Section 1) distinguishes deterministic and stochastic approaches, and the article positions Monte Carlo as a superior stochastic method for investment decisions.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: This foundational comparison sets the stage for understanding the need for Monte Carlo simulation, making it a teachable concept of appropriate scope.

reconciled_candidates.label: Sensitivity Analysis to Identify Key Risk Factors
reconciled_candidates.description: Sensitivity analysis uses tornado graphs and spider charts to rank risk factors by their impact on the output criterion, helping prioritize factors for risk management.
coverage_criteria: Interpret a tornado graph: identify the factor with the widest bar, explain quantile ranges, and determine direction of impact.
reconciled_candidates.merge_rationale: This candidate provides a focused method for analyzing which inputs most affect simulation outputs.

anchors.locator: 3.2. Sensitivity Analysis in the Simulation Model

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: Section 3.2 describes sensitivity analysis via tornado graphs and spider charts as part of the simulation environment, and Figures 4-7 provide visual examples.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: This is a specific analytical tool within Monte Carlo simulation, appropriate for a focused lesson on interpreting model outputs.

reconciled_candidates.label: Risk Mapping for Preliminary Risk Identification
reconciled_candidates.description: Risk mapping uses expert assessment to score probability and impact, creating a matrix that categorizes risks to guide quantitative analysis.
coverage_criteria: Create a risk matrix given a list of risks, assign probability and impact scores, and explain how the matrix informs subsequent simulation focus.
reconciled_candidates.merge_rationale: This candidate introduces a qualitative step that precedes simulation, identifying which risks are worth modeling.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: Section 3.1 presents risk mapping with a risk matrix (Figure 3) and explains how it led to selecting financial risks for the Monte Carlo simulation.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: Risk mapping is a distinct step before simulation, teachable as a separate qualitative technique.

reconciled_candidates.label: Project Comparison Using Simulation Statistics
reconciled_candidates.description: When comparing projects using simulation results, apply decision rules based on mean, standard deviation, coefficient of variation, and skewness to select the best project.
coverage_criteria: Compare two projects using mean, standard deviation, and skewness; explain which project is preferable and why; compute and interpret the coefficient of variation.
reconciled_candidates.merge_rationale: This candidate directly addresses how to translate simulation outputs into a business recommendation by comparing projects.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: Section 4 explicitly lists decision criteria for comparing two projects based on simulation statistics (Table 2), and applies them to select the A project.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: This concept encapsulates the actionable decision-making step that translates simulation outputs into a clear recommendation.

lesson.title: From Model Outputs to Business Recommendations
lesson.description: In this session, students learn how to translate the outputs of their Monte Carlo simulator into actionable business recommendations that a partner can understand and act upon. The lesson addresses one of the hardest transitions in data-driven decision-making, moving from a distribution of possible outcomes to a single defensible course of action. Students will examine the "flaw of averages" and why point estimates mislead executives, explore the six requirements of Decision Quality (appropriate frame, creative alternatives, relevant and reliable information, clear values and trade-offs, sound reasoning, and commitment to action), and practice articulating recommendations that explicitly acknowledge uncertainty, trade-offs, and confidence intervals.
